chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutakalli (may Allah have mercy on him) reported: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Adhniyah, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from al-Maimun al-Ban, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) being asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'He is the First and the Last.'

He said (peace be upon him): 'The First, not [meaning] a first that was before Him, nor a beginning that preceded Him; and the Last, not [meaning] an end as is understood in the attributes of created beings. Rather, He is Eternal, First, Last, who has always existed and will continue to exist, without beginning or end. Change does not befall Him, nor does He transition from one state to another, and He is the Creator of all things.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'He is the First and the Last' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that 'The First' and 'The Last' are not relative terms implying a predecessor or successor as with created beings, but denote His eternal existence without beginning or end. This explanation, found in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, emphasizes divine immutability and distinguishes God’s absolute eternity from the temporal limitations of creation. It serves as a foundational theological argument against anthropomorphism and temporal finitude in Shia creed.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1 - Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutakallim (rah) reported: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Adhniyah, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from al-Maimun al-Ban, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (as) being asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "He is the First and the Last."

He said: "The First, not preceded by any first, nor by any beginning that preceded Him, and the Last, not having an end as is understood in the attributes of created beings. Rather, He is the Eternal, the First, the Last, who has always existed and will continue to exist, without beginning or end. He does not experience change or transition from one state to another, and He is the Creator of all things."
